title: The Spirit, in Our Hearts
description: The Spirit, in Our Hearts in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 275 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Gospel Invitations”, where the book credits them to the Episcopal Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Spir-it, in our hearts, Is whis-pering, "Sin-ner, come!" The Bride, the Church of Christ, pro-claims To all his child-ren, "Come!"

lines: The Bride, the Church of Christ, proclaims
Let him that thirsts for righteousness,
And freely drink the stream of life;
Lord, even so! I wait thine hour:

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
